scope: Literary source text in the identified Gutenberg editions. No worldwide public-domain determination is made. Contributor introductions, translations and editorial prose are separate works; ancient originals alone do not clear modern translations.
method: Retrieved and parsed dcterms:rights from every listed Gutenberg RDF record. Checked catalog pages for disputed credits and cached title pages, prefaces and section credits for dates and attribution. Publication evidence quotes identify print editions, not Gutenberg release dates. A null publication_year means no print publication year was verified, not that the edition is copyrighted. Acceptance where the print date is unknown relies on Gutenberg's explicit U.S. determination, not an independently reconstructed copyright history.
hash_method: SHA256 of the exact bytes of scripts/inspiration/.cache/<id>.txt. These are the normalized source files produced by build.ts: decode UTF-8, remove a leading BOM, convert CRLF/CR to LF, remove text through the START marker and from the END marker onward when both markers exist, trim leading/trailing LF characters, append one LF, encode UTF-8. No quote cleaning, line joining or Unicode normalization is applied for these hashes.

general_evidence.finding: Gutenberg follows U.S. copyright law; U.S. public domain does not imply public domain elsewhere. It claims no copyright in markup, formatting or spelling modernization. Original copyright notices do not mean protection still exists.

Pre-1978 published works have a maximum 95-year copyright term. As of 2026, works published through 1930 have exhausted that term. More recent works may be public domain under other rules, but their publication date alone does not establish that.

use_decisions.public_domain_us_per_gutenberg: Accept literary text for U.S. use on Gutenberg's explicit public-domain determination. Print dates, when verified, provide additional evidence; no independent renewal/notice search was performed.
use_decisions.original_text_only: Accept the original literary text, but exclude the identified later introduction and its notes pending verification of their separate public-domain basis. This is a conservative project restriction, not a finding that Gutenberg's rights statement is false.
use_decisions.all_editions: Do not quote ebook production credits, transcriber/preparer commentary or modern editorial additions as if they were the original literature.

Wallis Budge; Egyptian Tales, edited by W. M. Flinders Petrie; Tell Amarna Tablets, C. R. Conder; other Egyptian texts credit Edouard Naville, Francois Chabas, C. W. Goodwin, Samuel Birch, F. C. attribution_corrections.correction: Credit F. Hadland Davis for the study and selection. Replace undifferentiated 'Various' with Reynold A. Nicholson (Divani Shamsi Tabriz), E. H. Whinfield (Masnavi) and William Hastie (the five Festival of Spring poems named in the preface). Rumi is the original poet, not the author of Davis's introduction or biographical prose.
attribution_corrections.cache_evidence: .cache/45159.txt:3-7,41-61: Davis explicitly identifies Nicholson, Whinfield and the late Rev. Professor Hastie and specifies the five Hastie poems.

attribution_corrections.correction: Zabelle C. Boyajian is compiler, illustrator and principal translator. Also name Alice Stone Blackwell and George M. Green as translators. Use the anthology's first-line index to credit each poem's actual author and translator, rather than blanket 'Various (Armenian)'. The collection also includes English work by John Gower and William Watson and Italian poems by Vittoria Aganoor Pompilj. James Bryce wrote the introduction; Aram Raffi wrote the historical contribution.
attribution_corrections.cache_evidence: .cache/54036.txt:1-18,55-87,7801-7899; index example: 'Unutterable silence here is spread', Raffi, translated by George M. Green (line 7876).

attribution_corrections.correction: These are authored ethnographic works, not wholly anonymous texts with the named writer solely a translator. Credit Washington Matthews, Frank Hamilton Cushing, Minnie Martin, Fay-Cooper Cole and Wilhelm Dittmer respectively as authors/collectors as appropriate; retain community origins for the embedded traditional material. Dittmer's title page says 'Orally collected and pictured'.
attribution_corrections.cache_evidence: The respective cached title pages name these writers; all five RDF records use dcterms:creator, not trl.

attribution_corrections.correction: Preserve traditional origins but distinguish collector/editor/translator prose from the tales. Chamberlain is cataloged as author; Matthews as compiler (title page: collected and translated); Cushing as author (title page: recorded and translated); Brinton as editor; Emerson as author (title page: collected and translated with notes); Busk as editor. A single blanket anonymous-author credit misattributes their introductions and scholarship.
The Irish anthology is not wholly anonymous: it includes named poets, and Lady Gregory wrote the introduction and English renderings. Credit original poets at passage level where identified.
attribution_corrections.cache_evidence: .cache/6656.txt:13-17,56-62 identifies translations by Gregory and quotes Davis's lament.
